plan.because: The supplied lease identifies the parties, premises and tenancy terms.
The dated letter identifies the reported shutter defects; receipt remains a separate issue.
The letter and customer report do not establish when the landlord received it.
Objective dated evidence of the affected shutters is needed.
Obtain the landlord's responses, proposed work and any access arrangements.
The customer explicitly denies damp or mould.
A heating fault is raised but unresolved; clarify whether heating is faulty before requesting a service report.
Health effects are unmentioned and presumed absent for planning.
A qualified examination is sought and the cause remains disputed. Request any available inspection findings.
The supplied letter identifies the recipient, repair deadline and proposed deposit; check its receipt and deposit safeguards separately.
This is optional under the process.

questions: Has the heating itself been checked or found faulty, or is the cold apparently coming through the shutters?
When did the landlord receive the 12 October letter, and do you have delivery or receipt evidence?
Is there any immediate safety concern from the broken shutters? Please provide any existing qualified inspection findings.
